answers.a: A rigid, non-porous plastic used in engineering.
answers.b: A crosslinked polymer network that soaks up water while holding its shape.
answers.c: A liquid suspension of polymers in oil.
answers.d: A type of crystalline metal alloy.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Hydrogels are porous and water-absorbing.
explanations.b: Correct — A hydrogel is defined as a crosslinked polymer network containing water.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Hydrogels are solid networks, not liquid suspensions.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Hydrogels are polymers, not metals.

questions.question: Q2. The swelling ratio Q is defined as:

answers.a: The swollen volume divided by the dry volume.
answers.b: The dry volume divided by the swollen volume.
answers.c: The mass of polymer divided by the mass of water.
answers.d: The rate at which water enters the gel.

explanations.a: Correct — Q = V_swollen / V_dry = 1 / v_p, where v_p is polymer volume fraction.
explanations.b: Incorrect — This is the reciprocal of Q.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Q is a volume ratio, not a mass ratio.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Q is an equilibrium ratio, not a rate.

questions.question: Q3. What does the Flory parameter χ represent in the Flory-Rehner equation?

answers.a: The crosslink density of the polymer.
answers.b: The temperature of the system in Kelvin.
answers.c: The solvent-interaction parameter; lower values mean the solvent loves water more.
answers.d: The molecular weight of the polymer chains.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Crosslink density is set by the V₁/V_e term.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Temperature is a separate input variable.
explanations.c: Correct — χ is the Flory solvent-interaction parameter; χ = 0.40 (Alginate) means water-loving, while χ = 0.55 (pHEMA) is less water-loving.
explanations.d: Incorrect — χ is an interaction parameter independent of chain length.

questions.question: Q4. In the self-folding gripper (Sub-Calc A), what physical phenomenon converts linear swelling into fold angle?

answers.b: A printed bilayer where the two materials swell differently.
answers.c: Surface tension at the water-polymer interface.
answers.d: Magnetic attraction to an external field.

explanations.a: Incorrect — The gripper uses mechanical swelling anisotropy.
explanations.b: Correct — A printed bilayer with different swelling ratios creates differential stress, causing the finger to fold (θ_fold ≈ 90° · (Q^(1/3) − 1)).
explanations.c: Incorrect — Surface tension is negligible at this scale.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The self-folding gripper is not magnetically actuated.

questions.question: Q5. The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation describes the:

answers.a: Rate of drug diffusion through the gel.
answers.b: Maximum load a gel can bear before rupture.
answers.c: Relationship between temperature and gel stiffness.
answers.d: Fraction of ionised groups on a weak polyacid as a function of pH.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Diffusion is described by the Korsmeyer-Peppas power law.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Mechanical failure is not described by Henderson-Hasselbalch.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Temperature-stiffness is described by rubber elasticity.
explanations.d: Correct — α = 1 / (1 + 10^(pKa − pH)) gives the ionisation fraction.

questions.question: Q6. What does LCST stand for, and at what temperature does it occur for PNIPAM?

explanations.a: Correct — The LCST (~32°C) is where PNIPAM-type gels collapse by expelling water.
explanations.b: Incorrect — The acronym and temperature are wrong.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Neither the acronym nor temperature is correct.
explanations.d: Incorrect — LCST is not a stabilisation regime.

questions.question: Q7. What is the dry shear modulus G_dry determined by?

answers.b: Only the temperature of the surrounding water.
answers.c: The number of elastically-effective chains per unit volume (ν_e) and thermal energy (k_B T).

explanations.a: Incorrect — Optical properties do not determine mechanical stiffness.
explanations.b: Incorrect — While T appears in the formula, ν_e (crosslink density) is equally important.
explanations.c: Correct — G_dry = ν_e k_B T according to affine rubber-elasticity theory.
explanations.d: Incorrect — pH affects ionic swelling, not the baseline dry modulus.

questions.question: Q8. How does swelling affect the Young's modulus of a gel?

answers.b: It remains constant regardless of swelling.
answers.c: It increases exponentially with the square of Q.
answers.d: It decreases as the cube root of Q (E ∝ Q^(-1/3)).

explanations.a: Incorrect — The relationship is not linear.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Swelling significantly softens the gel.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Modulus decreases with swelling, not increases.
explanations.d: Correct — G_swollen = G_dry · Q^(-1/3), and E = 3G for an incompressible gel.

questions.question: Q9. The Korsmeyer-Peppas power law (M_t / M_∞ = k t^n) is valid up to what fraction of drug released?

explanations.a: Incorrect — The model becomes unreliable earlier.
explanations.b: Correct — The Korsmeyer-Peppas power law is trustworthy only while the released fraction is less than 60%; beyond that, geometry and boundary effects dominate.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The model fails well before this.

questions.question: Q10. If the ionisation fraction f_ion is too high in a pH-triggered capsule, what is the failure mode?

answers.a: The shell over-swells and ruptures, dumping the entire dose at once.
answers.c: The capsule fails to open at any pH.
answers.d: The gel becomes insoluble and precipitates.

explanations.a: Correct — Excessive ionisation produces strong Donnan pressure; if Q exceeds ~24 the shell ruptures catastrophically.
explanations.b: Incorrect — The issue is premature over-swelling, not slow opening.
explanations.c: Incorrect — High ionisation actually increases opening.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Ionisation does not cause precipitation.
